patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Salesforce documents a broader use-case set; Zendesk Sell is narrower/specialist.

Salesforce documents a broader use-case set; Zendesk Sell is narrower/specialist. Choose Salesforce only if your buying job matches “Enterprise CRM platform for sales, service, marketing, and customer data across large and ” rather than Zendesk Sell's shape. Choose Zendesk Sell only if your buying job matches “Zendesk Sell CRM; Team $19 through Enterprise $169/agent/mo annual.” rather than Salesforce's shape. Workflow advantage: Salesforce leans account-management, complex-sales-processes; Zendesk Sell leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Salesforce documents a broader use-case set; Zendesk Sell is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Salesforce is Enterprise CRM platform for sales, service, marketing, and customer data across large and mid-market teams.; Zendesk Sell is Zendesk Sell CRM; Team $19 through Enterprise $169/agent/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: Salesforce (mid-market, enterprise) vs Zendesk Sell (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Salesforce-leaning account-management, complex-sales-processes, high-volume-lead-management vs Zendesk Sell-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Salesforce — USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite $100, Enterprise $175, Unlimited $350 per user/month (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from $125 Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO.; Zendesk Sell — Sell is one product in a larger Zendesk stack — packaging can confuse.

Limitations — Salesforce: USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite $100, Enterprise $175, Unlimited $350 per user/month (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from $125 Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO.; Premier Support is an add-on on Pro Suite. Agentforce for Sales, Sales Programs, Revenue Intelligence, and Revenue Cloud are separate paid add-ons; some require Contact us.; Zendesk Sell: Sell is one product in a larger Zendesk stack — packaging can confuse; Higher tiers escalate quickly vs SMB CRMs.

Poor-fit cases: Salesforce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite $100, Enterprise $175, Unlimited $350 per user/month (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from $125 Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO. · Zendesk Sell is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Sell is one product in a larger Zendesk stack — packaging can confuse · Avoid Salesforce if you actually need Zendesk Sell's motion (Zendesk Sell CRM; Team $19 through Enterprise $169/agent/mo annual.)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
